fixed_upstream.boundary: The packaged-client verifier and its harness are downstream internal workflow files and are absent from the fixed upstream tree.

findings.summary: Offline asset verification rescanned deep ancestors for every indexed object, making the first visible packaged-client scan unnecessarily slow.
findings.upstream_behavior: The fixed upstream commit predates these downstream packaged-client workflow scripts; no upstream verifier behavior is imported or changed by this remediation.
findings.incompatibility: The baseline verifier performed repeated Assert-PathUnder and Assert-NoReparsePathComponents walks inside the object loop. The canonical Player scan verified 4,750 assets, 453,637,622 bytes, and zero mismatches in about 594 seconds, with about 49 Get-Item guard calls per asset and about 232,750 total.
findings.replacement: Validate the derived objects root once, cache each existing or missing prefix directory once, probe each content-addressed leaf at most once, and stream the SHA-1 through .NET for the complete current run. Keep lexical root containment for index and object paths, direct reparse checks, missing/mismatch reporting, index and metadata identity, and logical indexed-object counts unchanged. No receipt is persisted across runs.
automated_evidence: The exact reviewed base 6bdd056fda18ae4a53ddf5d51a2edc50fe8576ff (tree b4b21301532f439f26d145ca4b85102acb16312f) was preserved; the implementation commit is e710757d88ecc5353be09907946ed3579ee28120 (tree 0b62ae9e0995f90ddd5d98b7e7a68f1d83a9adbf).

The verifier preserves full SHA-1 verification for every indexed object, lexical root containment, direct and ancestor reparse-point rejection, missing and mismatch reporting, metadata/index identity, path safety, exact logical object counts, exit propagation, and no persistent receipt cache.

Two complete performance-enabled harness runs passed with positive assets=4750, prefixGuards=256, leafGuards=4750, sha1Objects=4750, all 19 packaged-client negative cases including 13 asset-index-ID cases, and both Gradle hash-boundary negatives.

Offline Gradle check passed with verifyDependencyProvenance, offline clean jar passed, and audit-packaged-jar.ps1 passed deterministic archive equality with 498 entries, the expected client metadata, and the candidate SHA-256 recorded below.
The exact-base escape comparison and both final complete harness runs exited with the expected statuses; no current Player task, GUI, input, relaunch, or process inspection was performed.

findings.summary: Untrusted assetIndex.id could escape the canonical assets\indexes root through lexical parent traversal before the index was read.
findings.upstream_behavior: The fixed upstream commit predates these downstream packaged-client workflow scripts; no upstream verifier behavior is imported or changed by this remediation.
findings.incompatibility: At the exact reviewed base, an assetIndex.id containing three parent components derived an index path at assets\outside-parent.json. A valid-looking JSON object at that outside path was accepted with exit 0; Assert-NoReparsePathComponents rejected links but did not prevent lexical parent traversal.
findings.replacement: Treat assetIndex.id as an untrusted JSON string and require a non-empty, non-dot, single filename component with no separators, rooted/drive/UNC/device syntax, invalid filename characters, reserved device name, trailing dot/space, or excessive length. Canonicalize the existing assets\indexes root, assert the derived index path is lexically under that root before Test-Path, reparse, SHA-1, or JSON read, and retain root/index reparse checks.
automated_evidence: The exact reviewed base accepted the valid-looking outside-index JSON: BASE_ESCAPE_PASS exit=0; the derived path was assets\outside-parent.json, outside assets\indexes.
The candidate rejected the unchanged fixture before index existence/read: CANDIDATE_ESCAPE_REJECTED exit!=0 before index existence/read.

The candidate harness rejected deterministic backslash, forward-slash, and mixed-separator parent escapes, plus drive-rooted, UNC-rooted, device-rooted, empty, dot, dot-dot, reserved-device, trailing-dot, trailing-space, and invalid-character IDs.
A valid Minecraft-style ID 26.1.2-30 passed a positive preflight, while the three escape fixtures contained valid JSON outside assets\indexes and were rejected without being accepted as index input.
The two complete performance-enabled harness runs passed all 13 asset-index-ID negatives and both Gradle hash-boundary negatives with exit 0.
